title: Kernel offload & cache ops sync
body:
Meeting: Kernel offload + Cache ops weekly sync
Date: 2029-10-04
Attendees: Priya (owner), Lucas, Marisol, Ethan, Sasha (SRE join), QA: Dina (notes)
Purpose: Align on short-term kernel-offload prototype, results from KV async eviction experiments, and a rollout plan for batch-fusion scheduler.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Kernel offload shim prototype reduced per-token GPU memcpy by ~18% on 70B seq-256 traces but added ~6% CPU cycles; promising for memory-bound tails.
- KV-cache async eviction (staleness-window approach) increased effective cache hit-density from 62% -> 71% on our long-horizon chat traces, with small increase in tail latency on p95 due to occasional refetch.
- Batch-fusion scheduler (alpha) improves overall throughput for mixed sequence length workloads by ~12% when enabled with adaptive-split=on, but increases jitter; need canary and SLAs.

Notes and data highlights:
1) Kernel offload shim (PR #2124)
- What changed: Introduced an optional CPU-side accumulation stage for attention key/value deltas to avoid repeated large GPU->CPU memcpy during checkpointing and sparse updates. Shim is toggleable via runtime flag: kernel.offload_shim=true.
- Experiments: 70B model, seq_len distribution 64/128/256/512 (real traffic sample), steady-state QPS=120. Measured three runs each.
  - Baseline (no shim): avg token-latency 8.1ms, memcpy-per-token 240KB, GPU idle 5.2%
  - Shim enabled: avg token-latency 8.0ms, memcpy-per-token 197KB (-18%), CPU cycles +6%, GPU idle 3.8%
- Observations: tail latency p99 unaffected for short seq; p99.9 saw 0.6ms spikes under garbage collection windows on host machines.
- Open questions: should we add backpressure when host CPU >60%? How does shim behave on T4 vs L40?

2) KV cache async eviction (RFC-378)
- Implementation: eviction is now guided by a lightweight predictor (LRU+age-weighting) and executed asynchronously on worker threads with a staleness-window parameter (default 5s).
- Results (chat logs sample A, 30k sessions):
  - Hit-density (tokens served from KV vs total token-loads): baseline 62%, async-evict 71%
  - Cost delta: CPU work for eviction threads +9% overall CPU on p2 nodes; network egress unchanged.
  - Latency: median latency unchanged; p95 increased 5–12ms in 1.4% of requests where eviction coincided with heavy re-materialization.
- Decision point: Acceptance threshold: hit-density >= 68% and p95 tail < +15ms for canary. Current build passes hit-density but borderline on p95 for one region (eu-west-2).

3) Batch-fusion scheduler (alpha)
- Idea: Fuse small batches across model variants when sequence-length variance is high, using adaptive-split heuristics to maintain latency SLOs.
- Synthetic workload bench: mixed 7B+70B fleet, 30% long sequences (>256).
  - Fusion OFF: throughput 1.0x baseline
  - Fusion ON (adaptive-split=auto): throughput 1.12x, median latency +3ms, latency variance +18%
- Risks: jitter could violate stricter SLOs for customers on Dedicated. Requires route-level opt-in.

Action items (owners & rough ETA):
- Lucas: Add CPU backpressure gate to shim (threshold param + telemetry). ETA: 2029-10-11.
- Marisol: Run cross-region p95 sweep for KV async eviction (focus eu-west-2) and produce per-region p95 heatmap. ETA: 2029-10-09.
- Ethan: Canary pipeline for batch-fusion route opt-in; include golden prompts for regressions; tie to rollout flagging. ETA: 2029-10-14.
- Priya: Draft ops-runbook for shim failures + automatic disablement criteria. ETA: 2029-10-08.
- QA (Dina): Write 6 regression tests for cache re-materialization scenarios and add to nightly. ETA: 2029-10-10.

Decisions recorded:
- Proceed with a limited canary for KV async eviction in us-west-2 and us-east-1. If region p95 delta > +12ms at canary load, rollback.
- Kernel offload shim will be feature-flagged and disabled by default for Dedicated clusters until backpressure gating is in place.
- Batch-fusion to remain opt-in per-route; product will be notified to surface this to key customers.

Blockers and concerns:
- Observed GC-induced p99.9 spikes with shim on hosts that have older kernel/rt configurations; need infra checklist for host tuning. (SRE action: Sasha)
- Memory accounting: async eviction spikes temporarily increase working set; Ops needs headroom guidance for Dedicated customers. (Finance/PM outreach required)
- Telemetry gaps: no current metric for 'kv-evict-staleness' distribution; needs a short-term metric emitted from eviction controller.

Follow-ups / next sync agenda (2029-10-11):
- Lucas to demo backpressure gate and telemetry.
- Marisol to present regional p95 heatmap and propose rollback thresholds.
- Ethan to show canary pipeline plan and failure-mode simulations.
- SRE to share host-tuning checklist and recommended AMIs for shim-on fleets.

Appendix: quick notes and rough CLI snippets
- Toggle shim for local testing: REDWOOD_RUNTIME_FLAGS="kernel.offload_shim=true kernel.offload_backpressure=0.6" ./run-local
- Eviction debug: curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" $METRICS_HOST/debug/kv-evict?window=5
- Bench command: ./bench --model 70B --seq-dist sampleA.json --qps 120 --duration 10m --run-id shim-expt-20291004

Raw links & refs:
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2124
- RFC: RFC-378-kv-async-eviction (internal)
- Jira: SR-7891 (canary pipeline)

Notes to self (rough):
- If shim causes host GC > 3x baseline, flip flag off automatically. Might be easiest to implement in allocator.
- Consider a lightweight per-route knob in Console to opt-out of fusion for strict SLO customers.

End of sync.
